question: Can the Tooth-relic institution visible in Polonnaruwa be connected to Kandyan relic-based legitimacy without assuming an unchanged political mechanism across the intervening centuries?
mechanism: A durable, portable relic institution could survive changes of capital and dynasty, allowing later rulers to attach custodianship of the Tooth Relic to political legitimacy even though the actors, ritual forms and constitutional setting changed.
transmission_channel: institutional custody, relocation and ritual re-embedding of the Tooth Relic across royal capitals
time_lag: multi-century; Polonnaruwa evidence to early-modern Kandy
scale: Z1 institutional site to Z2 island-level kingship system
confounders: difference between relic protection and sovereign legitimacy
bounded_by: The bridge supports institutional persistence/portability as a plausible mechanism only. It does not establish uninterrupted annual Perahera continuity, identical sovereignty rules in every kingdom, or a direct causal line from the Velaikkara charter to Kandyan politics.
